items.title: TMA III Court Ruling Affirms Correct QPA Methodology: ASA's Work Referenced
items.reason: Court litigation directly interpreting the Qualifying Payment Amount (QPA) methodology is a core IDR topic per the rubric, as QPA determinations are fundamental to IDR eligibility and dispute resolution.
items.summary: A court ruling in TMA III affirmed the correct methodology for calculating the Qualifying Payment Amount (QPA), a critical metric in the No Surprises Act's IDR process that determines whether out-of-network disputes are eligible for independent dispute resolution. The decision referenced work by the American Surgical Association (ASA), indicating judicial validation of specific QPA calculation approaches. This ruling directly impacts how revenue-cycle teams and IDR entities assess dispute eligibility, as QPA calculations are a prerequisite gatekeeping function before cases can enter arbitration. The decision provides legal clarity on a contentious issue in IDR implementation and affects the scope of disputes that qualify for independent arbitration.
